title: Planner: Capacity view shows who is working on what
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's notice and the cited documentation. It correctly distinguishes the coarse Planner controls from a Capacity view switch and reports both the notice's Plan 3 wording and the service description's entitlement for existing Plan 5 subscribers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited service description and notice do not give a Plan 3 subscription price.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Capacity view price meter credits charge Plan 3 pricing. Read the complete Planner service description and supplied MC1474110; neither gives a Plan 3 price, and the service description links to a separate pricing page.

claims.claim: No Capacity view meter, credit rate or separate charge appears on the cited pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Capacity view price meter credits charge Plan 3 pricing. Read Planner service description, Planner for admins, manage-planner-app, disable-planner, Update-M365TeamsApp and MC1474110; none names a separate Capacity view meter, rate or charge.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: No dedicated Microsoft Learn page describing Capacity view's behaviour was found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "Capacity view"; Planner Capacity view documentation tenant admin disable switch PowerShell Microsoft Graph permissions rows edit tasks. Read service description and Planner for admins; the feature table names it but no dedicated feature page surfaced.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe which users within a plan see which Capacity view rows.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "Capacity view" "permissions"; Planner Capacity view permissions sign in plan membership rows Outlook Teams block app. Read service description, Planner for admins and Graph search excerpts; no Capacity view row-visibility rule surfaced.

claims.claim: The notice and Learn do not describe a Capacity view change to sign-in or permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Capacity view permissions sign in plan membership rows Outlook Teams block app; "Planner" "Capacity view" "permissions". Read MC1474110, service description and Planner for admins; none describes a Capacity view sign-in or permissions change.

claims.claim: The notice does not specify whether users can edit tasks from Capacity view.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Capacity view documentation tenant admin disable switch PowerShell Microsoft Graph permissions rows edit tasks. Read the supplied MC1474110 in full; it describes the timeline and data quality, not editing tasks from the view.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app for the organisation.
claims.quote: In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> to change an app's tenant state.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module; Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <String> [-IsBlocked <Boolean>]; -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Teams control blocks the whole Planner app at organisation level, rather than only Capacity view.
claims.quote: You can turn off or turn on the app at the org level on the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The cited Teams page does not say whether blocking Planner in Teams affects Planner in Outlook.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Capacity view permissions sign in plan membership rows Outlook Teams block app. Read manage-planner-app in full; Outlook references concern tasks, email and storage, not the effect of its Planner app block on Planner in Outlook.

claims.claim: No UI equivalent of the organisation-level IsPlannerAllowed setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner turn off organization IsPlannerAllowed admin center web user interface. Read disable-planner, Planner for admins and admin FAQ excerpts; results distinguish the Teams app block and Project settings, not a UI for IsPlannerAllowed.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is documented for turning off Planner for the organisation.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell. ... Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false

claims.claim: The cited Planner PowerShell instructions require a global admin.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.
